name: Rudbari
confidence_why: No source states where Rudbari main stress falls: Sabzalipour 2009, Stilo 1981 and Stilo 2001 say nothing about it, Lazard 1990 was not available, and Mirmiran and Alizadeh Jubani 2017 only note in passing that the second vowel of a hiatus and the plural, participle and relative-adjective suffixes carry stress, so the record remains undetermined.

new_statements.quote: یک نکته که شایسته توجه است این است که در گویش رودباری گاه دو واکه بدون میانجی در کنار یکدیگر قرار می‌گیرند که در این‌صورت واکه دوم همواره تکیه‌بر است. این تلاقی حتا ممکن است در یک واژه بسیط باشد مانند mâ'âr (مادر) و šâ'âl (شغال) که بواسطه همین تکیه و تمایز میان دو واکه از mâr (مار) و šâl (شال) تشخیص داده می‌شود. [p. 116:] اما اگر اسم به واکه‌های -e و -â ختم شود، در ساخت جمع، آن واکه با گردش واکی به o تبدیل می‌شود و سپس نشانه جمع به عنوان هجای تکیه‌بر به آن افزوده می‌شود. مانند: xone (خانه) ← xono'on (خانه‌ها)
new_statements.translation: One point worth noting is that in the Rudbari dialect two vowels sometimes stand side by side without a linking consonant, in which case the second vowel is always stressed. This hiatus can even occur inside a simple word, e.g. mâ'âr 'mother' and šâ'âl 'jackal', which are distinguished from mâr 'snake' and šâl 'shawl' precisely by this stress and by the distinctness of the two vowels. [p. 116:] But if the noun ends in the vowels -e or -â, in forming the plural that vowel changes to o by vowel alternation and then the plural marker is added to it as the stressed syllable, e.g. xone 'house' -> xono'on 'houses'.

new_statements.rule_in_words: The source gives no general word-stress rule; it states only that (i) in vowel hiatus the second (later) vowel is always stressed, even word-internally (mâ'âr, šâ'âl), (ii) the plural suffix -on is the stressed syllable of the plural noun, (iii) the past participle is formed with the stressed suffix -e, and (iv) hiatus present-tense verb forms (šo'om, ši'i, šu'u) stress the second syllable. These facts are consistent with word-final (suffix) stress in nouns but do not amount to a placement statement; Sabzalipour 2009 adds only that the adjective marker -a is an unstressed enclitic.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; Sabzalipour 2009 §2-3-1 notes the attributive marker -a is an unstressed enclitic (so not every final syllable is stressed).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level facts about isolated nouns (plural, participle, hiatus words) and verb forms in the Juboni (Jubon village, S. Rostamabad) variety of Rudbari Tati; no discussion of phrase-level or citation-form prosody. Stress marked only by the authors' statements, not by accent marks in transcriptions.
new_statements.identity_note: rudb1238 / ISO rdb = Rudbari of Rudbar county, Gilan (Sefid Rud valley; Glottolog coords 37.09N 49.88E; sole Glottolog ref Lazard 1990 'Le dialecte de Rudbâr (Gilân)'), locally called Tati-ye Rudbar(i); Stilo classifies it as a Tatic ('Tatoid') variety transitional to Gilaki. It must not be confused with (a) 'Rudbari' of southern Kerman (Rudbar-e Jonub/Kahnuj), a Garmsiri/Bashkardi variety that Persian Wikipedia gives ISO 'mis' and Glottolog nort2644, nor (b) Rudbaraki/Kelardashti (Mazandaran, Gilaki-related), nor (c) Tati of Rudbar-e Alamut (Qazvin). The quoted statement describes the Juboni variety (Jubon village, S. Rostamabad district, Rudbar county); Sabzalipour 2009 describes the Anbuh variety (Jirandeh, Amarlu district); both are Rudbar-Gilan varieties covered by rudb1238. Ethnologue's own location for rdb could not be verified (free page withholds it).

sources.note: p. 113: in vowel hiatus without a linking consonant the second vowel is always stressed (mâ'âr 'mother' vs mâr 'snake'; šâ'âl 'jackal' vs šâl 'shawl'); p. 116: plural marker -on is added 'as the stressed syllable' (xone -> xono'on); pp. 116-117: past participle formed with 'the stressed suffix -e'; p. 127: in hiatus verb forms (šo'om, ši'i, šu'u) the second syllable is stressed in all cases.
